newsitem.title: FRANCE: Georgia's Shevardnadze pays tribute to exiled prince.
newsitem.headline: Georgia's Shevardnadze pays tribute to exiled prince.

text.p: Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze visited France's St Cyr military academy on Wednesday to pay tribute to one of his countrymen, an exiled Georgian prince who died fighting for France in World War Two.

Shevardnadze, on an official visit, made a side trip to the St Cyr military academy at Coetquidan in Brittany to honour Prince Dimitri Amilakvari, a lieutenant colonel who commanded a Foreign Legion unit in the French Free forces in World War Two.
Amilakvari was killed at El Alamein in Egypt in 1942, aged 36, and Shevardnadze was to see the part of the academy's museum devoted to his memory.
A member of the Georgian royal house, Amilakvari left his homeland for exile in France with his parents in 1921 as the country fell under Communist rule.

He entered St Cyr and became a Legion officer, fighting rebels in Morocco before participating in the allied landings in Narvik, Norway, in 1940 and then joining General Charles de Gaulle's Free French movement in England.

Among agreements Shevardnadze signed in Paris on Tuesday was one for the training of Georgian military officers in France, although it was not immediately clear if they would be young cadets such as those trained at St Cyr.
Shevardnadze jokingly told the French daily Le Figaro that "Georgia's history is replete with men who died for the interests of other countries."
The current United States armed forces chief of staff, General John Shalikashvili, is the son of a Georgian officer who also fled the country when the Communists took over.
